brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Morning edition. It covers the 24 hours to 05:10 CET on 3 November; new research covers 17:10 CET on 2 November to 05:10 CET on 3 November, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Overnight Russian Barrage Hits Infrastructure in Dnipro and a Kharkiv Hospital
items.lede: Kharkiv's mayor said 25 people were hurt at a medical facility, and about 200 patients were being moved to other hospitals.

sections.text: Russia launched a large combined missile and drone attack on Ukraine overnight into Tuesday, Glavcom reported, citing Ukraine's air force [1]. The air force warned of ballistic missiles heading toward the Dnipropetrovsk, Vinnytsia, and Kharkiv regions [1]. Explosions were reported in Khmelnytskyi, Rivne, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, and Dnipro [1]. Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said Russia hit critical infrastructure in Dnipro and the Kryvyi Rih district [1]. Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov said 25 people were injured at a hospital [1]. Regional head Oleh Syniehubov said the strike hit a passage between hospital buildings in the Nemyshlianskyi district [1]. Terekhov had first reported four injured and heavy damage to the building, Interfax-Ukraine reported [2]. He said about 200 patients would be moved to other hospitals [1]. Residents of Zhytomyr reported power outages [1]. Ukraine's air force had not published a launch count by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on one live blog quoting officials. The attack was still under way at the cutoff, and figures are preliminary.

items.title: US Sets Ukraine-Russia Talks in Abu Dhabi for 10-11 November
items.lede: US envoy Steve Witkoff said Ukrainian and Russian delegations will meet in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November, with Witkoff and Jared Kushner expected to represent Washington.

sections.text: US envoy Steve Witkoff said Monday that the United States will bring Ukrainian and Russian delegations together in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November, Reuters reported [3]. He said the talks will cover post-war security agreements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures, and ending the war [3]. Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to represent the United States, a senior US official told Reuters [3]. US officials will also meet French, German, British, EU, and NATO representatives in Brussels this week on Ukraine's security guarantees, the official said [3]. Dutch broadcaster NOS also reported the Abu Dhabi talks early Tuesday [4]. No Ukrainian or Russian confirmation of the dates was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate because the dates come only from the US side, which Witkoff announced on the record, as Reuters reported. Kyiv and Moscow had not confirmed the dates by the cutoff.

items.title: Russian Bombs Kill 26 at an Aid Center in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia Region
items.lede: President Zelensky called it utterly horrific and said a second strike hit the place where people were sheltering after the first.

sections.text: At least 26 people were killed when Russian aerial bombs hit an aid distribution center in Komyshuvakha, in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, on Monday [5]. Regional head Mykhailo Semikin said at least nine 3,000-kilogram bombs hit the village [5]. He said five people were injured and 27 were initially reported missing [5]. Zelensky said the first strike hit a local school used to hand out aid [5]. Ukraine's emergency service confirmed 24 deaths, including two rescuers and four police officers [5]. Zelensky raised the toll to 26 in his late Monday video address [5][6]. He said Russia knew residents collected aid there every week [5]. No Russian Defense Ministry comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the strike and the toll, which BBC News attributes to Ukrainian officials and NOS also reported. The toll may still change.

items.title: Russian Strikes Leave 10 Ukrainian Regions Short of Power on Monday
items.lede: Overnight, Moscow sent 193 drones, and attacks over the past day killed two people, injured 32, and disrupted Kyiv's metro.

sections.text: Russia launched 193 attack and decoy drones at Ukraine from 18:00 Kyiv time on Sunday (17:00 CET), Ukraine's Air Force said [7][8]. Seventy-five of them were jet-powered Shaheds [7][8]. By 08:00 Kyiv time on Monday, air defenses had shot down or jammed 154 drones [7][8][9]. Drones hit 26 locations, and debris fell at nine more [7][9]. A strike on a five-story apartment building in Vasyshcheve, near Kharkiv, injured 12 people [10]. Four people were hurt when drones hit two apartment buildings in Odesa [10]. Over the past day, Russian attacks killed two people and injured 32 across Ukraine, officials said [9]. A drone hit a car in Sumy region and killed a 70-year-old woman [9]. The Energy Ministry said 10 regions had outages on Monday morning, with Dnipropetrovsk and Kyiv regions worst hit [9]. Power cuts disrupted Kyiv's metro and high-speed tram [9]. No Russian Defense Ministry statement on the strikes was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate on the drone totals, which are the Air Force's preliminary figures. Confidence is high on the casualties and outages, which officials reported on record.

items.title: Kremlin Rules Out New Front-Line Pauses After the Oleshky Evacuation Ends
items.lede: Kyiv and Moscow each accuse the other of regrouping during the six-day truce, while Washington puts the number of evacuees at nearly 800.

sections.text: Ukraine and Russia observed a local ceasefire around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in Ukraine's Kherson region, from 27 October [11][12]. US First Lady Melania Trump brokered the pause [13][14]. The truce expired at 22:59 Kyiv time on Sunday (21:59 CET) with no violations reported by either side [15]. Evacuees from the town crossed into Ukraine's Chernihiv region on Saturday, Zelensky said [16]. A Ukrainian official told AFP that Russia refused Kyiv's offer to extend it [15][17]. On Monday, Melania Trump said on X that nearly 800 people were evacuated [18]. Ukraine's ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, said the agreement bars both sides from releasing their own figures [18]. Ukraine's General Staff said Russia used the pause to rotate units, strengthen positions, and bring in ammunition [19]. Lubinets said Russian vehicles seen in Sky News footage were doing demining under Ukrainian supervision [19]. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the operation a success and thanked Melania Trump [20][21]. He said Russia has no plans for similar pauses elsewhere on the front [20][21]. He said Ukrainian forces likely used the pause to regroup [20][21].
Confidence is high on what Peskov, Lubinets, and Melania Trump said, which is on record. The evacuee total rests on Melania Trump alone, and each side's buildup claims are not independently verified.

items.title: Zelensky Offers to Halt Refinery Strikes if the US Sells Ukraine Patriots
items.lede: Kyiv's leader tied any pause to faster US interceptor deliveries, saying Ukraine would pay for a month of missiles and hold fire for the same month.

sections.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told Fox News on Sunday that Ukraine would stop striking Russian oil refineries if the United States quickly supplied Patriot interceptors [17][22]. He said a month of missile deliveries would buy a month without refinery strikes [17][22]. He said Ukraine would pay for the missiles rather than rely only on aid [17]. He said Ukraine would also halt the strikes if Russia stopped attacking Ukraine's energy system [17][22]. The US State Department approved a possible $2.1 billion sale of Patriot interceptors to Ukraine on 30 October [17][23]. Zelensky has warned that deliveries of the 500 interceptors could take years [17][22]. A State Department official told European Pravda on Monday that deliveries are expected from late 2030 to late 2033 [23][24]. President Trump, facing soaring energy prices at home, has pressed Kyiv to stop refinery strikes [17][22]. No White House or Kremlin response was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on what Zelensky said, because RFE/RL and the Guardian quote the Fox News interview directly. The delivery window rests on one unnamed official. The interview's exact broadcast time is not established.

items.title: Russia's Military Says Its Troops Took Barilovka in Ukraine's Sumy Region
items.lede: Moscow also claimed gains in four other Ukrainian regions, while Kyiv's military said Russian troop losses on Sunday hit a one-day record.

sections.text: Russia's Defense Ministry said units of its North group captured the village of Barilovka in Ukraine's Sumy region [25]. It said the 41st Motor Rifle Regiment took the village after artillery and drone strikes, and troops are now clearing mines [25]. In its daily summary, the ministry said its forces improved positions in the Kharkiv, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Dnipropetrovsk regions [26]. It also said air defenses downed 658 Ukrainian drones over the past day [26]. Ukraine's General Staff said Russia lost a record 2,500 troops on 1 November [27]. It puts total Russian losses since February 2022 at 1,592,770 troops [27]. No Ukrainian statement on Barilovka was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is low on the capture of Barilovka, which rests on Russia's Defense Ministry alone and was not independently verified. Both sides' loss figures are their own unverified claims.

items.title: Zelensky Says He Is Ready to Meet Putin in Turkey
items.lede: Kyiv's leader wants Abu Dhabi technical talks to set up a later summit on a full ceasefire, and he rejects ceding occupied land.

sections.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told CNN Turk that he is ready to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Turkey [28]. The interview was published on Sunday [28]. Zelensky called a leaders' meeting essential and said Turkey could be a practical mediator [28]. He said technical talks with Russia and the United States in Abu Dhabi would cover a partial energy and maritime ceasefire [28]. He said those talks would also cover prisoner exchanges [28]. A later leaders' summit would address a full ceasefire and security guarantees, he said [28]. He rejected recognizing occupied land as Russian and called for a ceasefire along the current front line [28]. He met Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Istanbul on 31 October [28]. No Kremlin response to the offer was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because only one outlet's account of the interview was read. The interview's exact publication time is not established.

items.title: Ukrainian Drones Reportedly Hit Russia's Samara Oil Pumping Hub
items.lede: Samara's governor said only that the region was repelling a Ukrainian attack, and no damage assessment or casualty report was found by the cutoff.

sections.text: Drones attacked the Samara oil pumping and dispatch station near Prosvet in Russia's Samara region early Monday, Russian outlet Astra and Ukrainian monitoring channels reported [29][30]. Residents reported explosions and a column of smoke rising from the site, Astra said [29]. Samara Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said only that the region was repelling a Ukrainian attack [29]. Russia's Defense Ministry said air defenses downed 212 drones over Russian regions overnight, including over Samara region [29]. The station blends crude for shipment through Russia's main oil pipelines, and Astra calls its tank farm Europe's largest [29][30]. It lies about 835 kilometers (520 miles) from Ukraine's border [30]. Ukrainian drones hit the same site in early October [29][30]. No Ukrainian military claim, casualty report, or damage assessment was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate that drones attacked the site, because the governor confirmed an attack on the region and two outlets cite local footage. Confidence is low on any damage, which no official has confirmed.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Hackers Warm Supermarket Freezers in Belgium and Eight Other European Countries
items.lede: Belgian federal prosecutors opened a criminal case as stores dumped spoiled food, and no group had claimed the attack by Monday afternoon.

sections.text: A cyberattack overnight into Monday hit fridges and freezers in dozens of supermarkets across Europe [1]. AFP reported early Tuesday that stores in at least nine European countries were hit, including Italy and Portugal [2]. About 40 Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected [1]. Fewer shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia, and Finland [1][3]. Carrefour said 15 of its roughly 700 Belgian stores were affected [1][3]. Ireland's SuperValu said 13 of its 233 stores were hit [3]. Belgian refrigeration firm Sabcobel said units were switched to defrost mode, the method believed used in an October attack in France [1]. A Belgian ethical hacker told VRT the attackers used a known flaw in Danfoss equipment [4]. Belgium's federal prosecutor's office opened a criminal investigation, a spokesperson said [5][4]. EU Agriculture Commissioner Christophe Hansen called the attacks a deliberate attempt to disrupt the EU food supply [3]. No group had claimed the attack, and no government named a culprit by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the attack, the countries hit, and the Belgian criminal case, which the BBC, The Guardian, VRT, and Reuters report from company, prosecutor, and EU statements. The Danfoss flaw rests on one outside expert quoted by VRT.

items.title: Ukraine Partly Restores Its Air Raid App After Fake Nuclear Alerts
items.lede: Developers turned warnings back on Monday but kept target tracking off, and the Air Force said the late-Sunday hack did not affect military operations.

sections.text: Ukraine's Air Alert app sent false warnings late Sunday, the Ukrainian Air Force said [6][7]. Messages warned of radiation and chemical threats in Kyiv and of street fighting in the capital [6][7]. The Air Force said the app had probably suffered hostile interference and that there was no radiation threat [6][8]. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications blamed Russia in a post on X [7][9]. Early Monday, Russia's Emergencies Ministry said its mobile app suffered a massive cyberattack that let attackers send false information [7][9]. A Ukrainian partisan group, Atesh, shared what it said was a screenshot of a fake nuclear strike warning sent to Russian users, the BBC reported [6]. On Monday, the app's developers said they had partly restored the service and resumed push alerts [10]. Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat said the hack did not affect Ukraine's defense forces or its own alert channels [11]. Zelensky told PBS News on Monday that Ukraine had hacked back after the attack on its alert system [12]. "We only respond on their attacks," he said [12].

Confidence is high that both apps sent false alerts, based on official statements reported by the BBC, Al Jazeera, DW, and ABC. The restoration rests on the developers' statement via dev.ua. No attribution has been independently confirmed.

items.title: Polish Police Launch Special Operation on Kaliningrad Border Over Sabotage Warnings
items.lede: Poland's national police chief said the operation follows signals of possible sabotage, with counterterrorism officers sent to two northeastern provinces to work with army and Border Guard units.

sections.text: Poland's national police chief, Marek Boroń, said police set up a special operation along the border with Russia's Kaliningrad exclave [13]. He said the move followed signals that acts of sabotage could take place there in the coming days [13][14]. Extra officers, including counterterrorism units, went to the Warmia-Masuria and Podlasie provinces [14]. Police are working with the army, the Border Guard, and the security services, with command at national police headquarters [13]. Boroń linked the operation to sabotage and the actions of eastern intelligence services [13]. RMF reported that Polish military intelligence and allied agencies warned last week of possible border violations by armed groups [13][14]. A police spokeswoman told TVN that operational details were confidential [14]. No Russian or Belarusian response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that the operation exists, because the national police chief described it on record to RMF. The intelligence warning about armed groups rests on unnamed sources cited by RMF.

items.title: Britain Deploys the RAF to Jersey After Weekend Airport Drone Incursions
items.lede: The UK Ministry of Defence confirmed the military deployment to a specialist outlet, while island police were still hunting the drone operators on Monday.

sections.text: Unauthorized drones flew in restricted airspace near Jersey Airport on Friday evening, disrupting flights from Britain to the British Crown Dependency [15]. The first report came at about 20:20 local time (21:20 CET), and further drone activity was reported until about 22:30 (23:30 CET), the Jersey Evening Post reported [16]. Jersey Police Inspector Rob McCallum said officers believed two or three drones had been in the restricted airspace [15]. On Saturday at 21:05 CET, the airport reported fresh drone disruption to inbound flights [17][18]. No disruption to Sunday evening's flights was reported, the BBC said late Sunday [19]. Britain's Ministry of Defence told sUAS News that the Royal Air Force had deployed to Jersey [20]. It said the RAF was answering a request for military aid to civil authorities, with the Department for Transport leading counter-drone work [20]. Police kept searching for the drone operators on Monday and asked islanders for sightings and footage [21]. No operator, motive, or state link was named by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on both nights of disruption and the quiet Sunday evening, which the BBC, Channel 103, and the Jersey Evening Post reported from official statements. The RAF deployment rests on one specialist outlet citing the UK Ministry of Defence. The drone count rests on one police estimate.

theaters.heading: Politics, security, and defense across the EU and NATO's European members

items.title: Czech Public Broadcasters Cut News Programs for Tuesday's Strike Over Funding
items.lede: Staff at Czech Radio and Czech Television say the government's plan to fund them from the state budget threatens their independence.

sections.text: Czech Radio said Monday it will scale back news and current affairs programs during a one-day staff strike on Tuesday [1]. Music, repeats, and archive shows will replace regular programs on several national and regional stations [1]. The broadcaster said it would keep basic news coverage and inform the public in an emergency [1]. Veřejnoprávně, a group representing Czech Radio and Czech Television employees, called the strike [1][2]. It opposes the governing coalition's plan to abolish license fees and fund both broadcasters from the state budget [1][2]. A group spokesman said the strike would affect all Czech Television channels, most visibly the news channel ČT24 [2]. Czech Television said its ČT24 news channel would switch to reduced programming at midnight, with a short news bulletin every hour [3]. Its main evening newscast and morning show will not air [3].
Confidence is high on the strike and its cause, per Czech Radio's English service and ČT24. Both outlets belong to the striking broadcasters.

items.title: France's High School Blockades Resume as Paris Police Ban a Student March Route
items.lede: Monday's school protests follow 779 arrests at Saturday's marches, and five unions plan a national strike on Thursday.

sections.text: France's third Saturday of cost-of-living protests drew 320,000 people nationwide, including 70,000 in Paris [4][5]. The Interior Ministry said police had arrested 565 people nationwide by 21:00 [5][6]. By 21:00, Paris police had made 79 arrests in the Paris area [5]. Prosecutors opened an attempted-homicide investigation on Sunday after Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez called the firebombing attempted murder [4][7]. The Interior Ministry said the IGPN and IGGN police watchdogs had received 83 cases since student protests began in mid-September, franceinfo reported [8]. One involves a Reims marcher whose shin was seriously injured by a police grenade [9]. On Sunday, the Interior Ministry put the final count at 779 arrests and 116 officers hurt [10]. France's Education Ministry said 41 high schools were blocked Monday, while a student union counted more than 150 [11]. Paris police on Monday banned Tuesday's student march route from the Panthéon to Medef headquarters, offering an alternative from Porte de Charenton to Porte de Montreuil [12]. Organizers rejected it and said they would challenge the order in court [12]. The prefecture's curfew order n° 2026-01485 for the République and Châtelet-Les Halles sectors expired at 06:00 Monday [13][14]. A planned 0.8% riot insurance surcharge from 2027 still needs Conseil d'État validation [15].
Confidence is high on turnout, arrests, and clashes, per franceinfo, the Guardian, and RTBF.

items.title: Czech Cabinet Adopts a 2040 Army Plan That President Pavel Says Falls Short
items.lede: Pavel said the concept would not meet NATO commitments or prepare the army for a high-intensity conflict, and Prime Minister Andrej Babiš pushed back.

sections.text: The Czech government approved a new army development concept through 2040 on Monday, Prime Minister Andrej Babiš said [16]. The cabinet also adopted a long-term defense outlook through 2045 [16]. President Petr Pavel attended the cabinet session to discuss both documents [17]. Afterward, Pavel told reporters the plan would not ensure the country meets its allied commitments [16][17]. He said it also would not prepare the army for a high-intensity conflict [16][17]. The concept says planned funding of 2% of GDP through 2030 allows only limited development of selected capabilities [16]. Its priorities include completing a heavy brigade, air and counter-drone defense, and better command and control [16]. Babiš said he could not imagine a major conflict in which Russia attacks the country [16]. Defense Minister Jaromír Zůna said building the army is not a race over percentages [16].
Confidence is high on the approval and Pavel's criticism, per ČTK and Radio Prague International.

items.title: Belgium's King Holds De Wever's Resignation and Summons Coalition Leaders
items.lede: King Philippe will see all five party leaders from Tuesday and meet the prime minister again on Friday, warning against a long crisis.

sections.text: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever offered his government's resignation to King Philippe on Monday morning after budget talks collapsed [18][19]. The palace said the king was withholding his decision [18]. The king will meet the leaders of the five coalition parties from Tuesday to Thursday and see De Wever on Friday at 10:30 CET [18]. A palace statement regretted the lack of a credible budget deal and urged the partners to compromise [18]. The king said Belgium cannot afford a long political crisis amid geopolitical and economic uncertainty [18]. The inner cabinet had failed overnight to agree on a federal budget, Deputy Prime Minister David Clarinval said [20][21]. The coalition is trying to find 10 billion euros in savings by 2029 [21]. Without a budget, the government would have to run on monthly stopgap spending [21].
Confidence is high on the resignation offer, the king's response, and the consultation schedule, per RTBF and El País citing the palace.

items.title: EU's Kallas Tells Britain to Join Defense Programs Before Any Rejoining Talks
items.lede: Meeting UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting before the 20 November summit, the EU foreign policy chief said some in the EU remain traumatized by Brexit.

sections.text: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Britain should first take part in existing EU defense frameworks rather than open talks on rejoining the bloc [22]. She spoke Monday in Brussels at a meeting with UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting [22]. The talks come before an EU-UK summit on 20 November [22]. Kallas said negotiations would be difficult and urged a step-by-step approach [22]. She said some in the EU are still traumatized by the bitter Brexit negotiations [22]. Streeting also met EU Defense Commissioner Andrius Kubilius [22]. Streeting said Britain remains committed to closer defense cooperation with the EU [22]. Britain stayed out of the EU's 150 billion euro SAFE defense loan program last year after a dispute over the entry fee [22]. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has not ruled out talks on Britain rejoining the EU [22].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on Euronews alone. Deutschlandfunk and ABC headlines reported the same remarks, but their pages were not read.

items.title: Spain's Cabinet to Approve Aid for Urda Train Crash Victims on Tuesday
items.lede: Four Americans were among the 69 dead, and Pedro Sánchez vowed to restore trust in high-speed rail whatever it costs.

sections.text: Spain's victim identification body said late on Sunday that four US citizens were among the 69 people killed in Wednesday's crash near Urda [23]. One victim each came from Canada, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Tunisia, and the Czech Republic, the Guardian reported [23]. Officials had already confirmed 54 Spaniards, one French citizen, and one Portuguese citizen among the dead [23]. A Renfe train hit a stationary Iryo train about 130 km south of Madrid [23]. A control center let the Renfe train move after a safety system halted traffic [23]. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said on Monday that his cabinet will approve an aid package for victims on Tuesday [24]. The plan doubles mandatory accident insurance payouts and advances compensation to victims [24]. Sánchez said the crash, which also injured 34 people, should never have happened [24]. He said Spain must restore trust in high-speed rail as soon as possible, whatever it costs [24]. The crash comes before Spain's 29 November general election [23].
Confidence is high on the aid plan, per El País. Confidence is moderate on the victims' nationalities, which rest on the Guardian alone.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Latvia's Kulbergs Ends First Round of Coalition Talks Without a Cabinet Deal
items.lede: The premier warns of serious budget cuts, Latvia First's Šlesers pledges support for unpopular reforms, and Kulbergs's formal nomination is expected 4 November.

sections.text: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs finished a first round of government talks on Monday with no deal on a cabinet, Latvian Radio reported via LSM [1]. His last meeting was with Latvia First, the second-largest party with 17 seats [1]. Kulbergs said Latvia must make serious budget cuts and review the number of ministries [1]. Latvia First leader Ainārs Šlesers compared the country's finances to the sinking Titanic [1]. Šlesers said his party would vote for unpopular reforms whatever government Kulbergs forms [1]. He did not say whether he would back a government without his party [1]. Kulbergs said every coalition option remains open, including a minority government [1]. He will not invite the Sovereign Power alliance, citing opposite views on security and Ukraine [1]. The new parliament meets for the first time on 3 November, and Kulbergs's formal nomination as prime minister is expected on 4 November [1].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one Latvian Radio report published by LSM; the quotes rest on that report.

items.title: Hackers Set an Estonian Supermarket Freezer to 50 Degrees Celsius
items.lede: The Selver chain says the store suffered no damage, and a refrigeration contractor says the method matches October attacks on supermarkets in France and the Netherlands.

sections.text: A cyberattack hit one store of Estonia's Selver supermarket chain on Monday morning, ERR reported [2]. Hackers reached a computer that controls refrigeration and changed a freezer setting to 50 degrees Celsius [2]. Jann Mutso, head of refrigeration firm Kitman Coldtech, said the attackers entered an older Danfoss control system [2]. He said other clients in Estonia were also attacked [2]. ERR said similar incidents were reported Monday in Sweden, Belgium, and Luxembourg [2]. Selver spokeswoman Mariann Järvela said the contractor spotted the attack quickly and the store suffered no damage [2] [3]. She said it was the last Selver store still using the old system [2]. No one has claimed the attack, and no Estonian government attribution was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: ERR reported the Estonian attack, and LSM's account draws largely on ERR; the attacks in other countries were not checked at their source.

items.title: Estonia's Chancellor of Justice Faults the Military Over a Reservist's Background Check
items.lede: The watchdog gave the defense minister one month to report back after the army barred a reservist with an archived criminal record from training Ukrainian troops.

sections.text: Estonia's Office of the Chancellor of Justice ruled that the Defense Forces acted illegally when they barred a reservist over his criminal record, ERR reported Monday [4]. The army and the Defense Resources Agency had refused to let him join the Legio mission that trains Ukrainian soldiers [4]. Office director Olari Koppel said the army's check of the man's archived criminal record broke the law [4]. He said the man got unclear and inaccurate information about the selection process [4]. The office said the army may still choose whom it brings in, but a refusal needs specific reasons and a clear legal basis [4]. It asked the defense minister to report within one month [4].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one ERR report quoting the office's ruling; the ruling itself was not read.

items.title: Estonia Expels a Russian Academic Its Security Service Ties to Moscow's Spy Agencies
items.lede: Police walked Leonid Karabeshkin, a former Tallinn professor and ERR employee, to the Koidula border crossing, and he now faces a Schengen entry ban.

sections.text: Estonian police expelled Russian citizen Leonid Karabeshkin early Monday at the request of the Internal Security Service, known as KAPO, ERR and Postimees reported [5] [6]. KAPO said the expulsion aims to prevent activities that threaten the security of Estonia and Europe [5]. Police also revoked his residence permit and banned him from entering the Schengen area [5] [6]. KAPO posted a video on X showing two officers escorting a man to the Russian border at Koidula in southern Estonia [5]. Karabeshkin taught at the now-closed Euroacademy in Tallinn and worked at ERR for two years [5]. KAPO spokeswoman Marta Tuul said he had contacts with Russian intelligence services and met them during regular trips to Russia [5]. She said he shared information with them about Estonia's Russian-speaking population [6]. She linked him to the influence networks CIRP, RuBaltic, and Regnum [5]. No Russian statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the expulsion: ERR and Postimees both report it from KAPO's statement; the intelligence claims are KAPO's alone and were not independently checked.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the Western Balkans

items.title: Serbia's Rerun Gives Zukorlić's Party a Seat, Observers Say
items.lede: Official commission figures put the Student List at 53% nationwide, and Vučić pledged his lawmakers would not block the new parliament.

sections.text: Serbia held repeat voting on Sunday at 53 polling stations, part of the 25 October snap parliamentary election, N1 reported, citing the observer group CRTA [1]. CRTA said observers recorded isolated vote-buying, parallel voter lists, and unauthorized people at and outside polling stations [1]. Late Sunday, the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) published results from all 8,392 polling stations [2] [3]. The Student List won 53.01%, and Aleksandar Vučić's United Serbia list won 38.98% [2] [3]. Usame Zukorlić's SPP list won 0.28% [2]. RIK now has 96 hours to publish final results, which start the clock to convene the new parliament [3]. By CRTA's count, the rerun gives SPP one seat and cuts the Student List to 140, with Vučić's list on 103 [4]. CRTA said 12 votes decided the SPP seat [4]. Zukorlić said his list won more than 300 votes at the rerun stations [5]. Prosecutors in Aleksinac opened a case over social media posts alleging vote-buying for Zukorlić's list at a polling station in Glogovica [6]. Vučić told TV Pink his lawmakers would not obstruct the parliament's formation and would take part in its work [7].
Confidence is high on the vote shares, which Tanjug and N1 both relay from RIK; confidence is moderate on the seat split, which rests on CRTA's own projection.

items.title: Serbian Police Arrest Alta Bank Owner Over Missing 385 Million Euros
items.lede: Prosecutors say about 385 million euros left the vault, two staff helped him, and the crisis has spread to a subsidiary in North Macedonia.

sections.text: Serbia's owner of Alta Bank, Davor Macura, was arrested Monday, three days after the National Bank of Serbia revoked the bank's license [8]. Organized crime prosecutors suspect he took about 45 billion dinars, nearly 385 million euros, from the bank's vault [8]. Two treasury staff were also arrested on suspicion of letting him into the vault with access cards [8]. The National Bank revoked the license on 31 October, citing worsening finances and liquidity concerns [8]. North Macedonia's stock exchange put the subsidiary Alta Bank Bitola on its watch list Monday [9]. No statement from Macura or his lawyers was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the arrest and prosecutors' allegations rest on BIRN's report of the prosecution statement; the Bitola listing comes from Beta via N1.

items.title: Kosovo Loses 43.8 Million Euros in EU Growth Plan Funds After Missed Reforms
items.lede: The chief negotiator blamed nearly two years of political deadlock, and another 131.5 million euros hinges on 22 reforms due by year's end.

sections.text: Kosovo's chief EU negotiator, Jeton Zulfaj, told a parliamentary committee Monday that the country lost 43.8 million euros in EU Growth Plan funding [10]. He said Kosovo carried out seven of 13 reform steps by the June 2026 deadline and missed six [10]. Most of the missed steps needed parliamentary approval, including energy and bankruptcy laws, a justice package, and an organized crime strategy [10]. Kosovo has gone through nearly two years of deadlock and three parliamentary elections in a row [10]. Zulfaj said the measures are back before parliament and should pass this year [10]. Another 22 reforms worth 131.5 million euros are due by 31 December [10]. A final European Commission decision is expected in the coming days [10]. No Commission comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the figures rest on Zulfaj's briefing as reported by BIRN's Prishtina Insight; a Kosovo Online report on the loss returned no readable text.

items.title: Albanian Students March Through Tirana Campuses on Day 21 of Protests
items.lede: Protesters walked into lecture halls urging classmates to join a boycott, while Edi Rama renewed his offer of talks but ignored demands that he resign.

sections.text: Albanian students marched Monday through Tirana, the capital, on the 21st day of protests and a class boycott demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation [11]. The march began at the Academy of Arts and moved to the law school and the natural sciences faculty [11]. Protesters entered the law faculty and urged other students to join the boycott [11]. The marchers end each day at the Education Ministry [11]. Rama again invited the protesters to talk, placing paper signs with that message on a stone table [11]. Teachers and professors have joined the daily protests, which began on 13 October [11]. Earlier clashes saw protesters throw stones and Molotov cocktails, and police respond with tear gas and water cannons [11]. No police statement on Monday's march was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: Monday's march rests on one regional outlet relaying Euronews Albania and Newsmax Balkans; no arrests or clashes were reported for Monday.

items.title: Iliana Iotova Wins Bulgaria's Presidential Runoff With 57.6% of the Vote
items.lede: With every precinct counted Monday morning, she finished ahead of rival Andrey Gyurov by about 344,000 ballots, and certified figures are due within three days.

sections.text: Bulgaria's Central Election Commission (CIK) finished processing 100% of precinct protocols from Sunday's presidential runoff by 09:00 Sofia time (08:00 CET) Monday, BNR reported [12]. Iliana Iotova and running mate Kiril Valchev won 57.566%, or 1,093,852 votes [12]. Andrey Gyurov and Georgi Kandev won 39.483%, or 750,251 votes [12]. Another 2.951% marked "I do not support anyone" [12]. Iotova lost only three districts in Bulgaria: Kardzhali and Sofia's 23rd and 24th [12]. Abroad, Gyurov led overall, but Iotova carried voters in Spain, Cyprus, Russia, and North Macedonia [12]. Iotova is set to become Bulgaria's first elected woman president, RTÉ reported [13]. Gyurov said he accepted the results, "however surprising they might be" [14]. Iotova said Gyurov called to congratulate her [15]. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen congratulated her on X [13]. Turnout was 29.1%, BIRN reported [16]. Iotova campaigned on a more balanced line toward Russia and skepticism about more military aid to Ukraine [16]. CIK must announce official final results within three days of election day [17] [12]. Police logged 461 reports of suspected violations by midafternoon Sunday, mostly about vote-buying [18].
Confidence is high: the full count, relayed by BNR, matches earlier CIK partial data, BTA, and RTÉ's wire-based report; figures stay preliminary until CIK certifies them.

items.title: Container From Drone-Sunk Ship Likely Washes Ashore on Bulgaria's Coast
items.lede: Military prosecutors opened a case and guards watch the box near Burgas while officials check its contents, which preliminary data suggest are not hazardous.

sections.text: A shipping container washed ashore Monday on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast between Arapya campsite and the Oasis resort, Burgas regional governor Diko Dikov said [19]. The alert came in around 08:00 Sofia time (07:00 CET) [19]. Dikov said the container is likely part of the cargo of the sunken ship Contship Jet, owned by a Liberian company [19]. Preliminary data show no sign of hazardous cargo, but Dikov called that an assumption [19]. Military prosecutors in Sofia opened a pretrial case, and military police are guarding the container around the clock [19]. On Sunday, Bulgaria's vessel traffic service warned ships about four containers drifting east of Burgas Bay, BTA reported [20]. On 28 October, three maritime drones struck a container ship about 21 nautical miles southeast of Shabla, and it sank around midnight [20]. Navy commander Rear Adm. Kiril Mihaylov said 20 of its 421 containers fell overboard [20].
Confidence is moderate: Monday's landing rests on the governor's remarks in one outlet, and Sunday's warning rests on BTA; the cargo link is the governor's assumption.

items.title: Georgia and Azerbaijan Agree to Speed Up Talks on Their Disputed Border
items.lede: Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze said 15 sections remain unresolved, including the area around the David Gareji monastery complex.

sections.text: Georgia and Azerbaijan agreed Monday to accelerate the delimitation and demarcation of their shared border, Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze said [1]. He spoke after the two countries' intergovernmental economic cooperation commission met in Georgia for the 11th time [1]. Azerbaijani Prime Minister Ali Asadov co-chaired the session [1]. Kobakhidze said there had been no progress in recent years and 15 sections remained unresolved [1]. The disputed areas include the David Gareji monastery complex [1]. The two sides signed cooperation documents on customs and agriculture [1]. Asadov said Azerbaijan is Georgia's largest investor, with nearly $4 billion invested [1].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on one regional news digest; Rustavi 2 headlines on the meeting were seen but not read.

items.title: Georgian Appeals Court Cuts a Tbilisi Protester's Seven-Year Sentence in a Plea Deal
items.lede: Nana Sander, convicted over the 4 October 2025 unrest, is due for release on 6 November after pleading guilty.

sections.text: A Georgian appeals court approved a plea deal Monday for Nana Sander, convicted over the 4 October 2025 unrest in Tbilisi [2]. Judge Paata Silagadze cut her seven-year sentence to one year and one month, plus a two-year suspended term [2]. She is due for release on 6 November [2]. A lower court had convicted her in June of organizing group violence [2]. The judge upheld the sentences of two co-defendants, Mariam Mekantslishvili and Abo Naveriani [2]. Naveriani received five years in prison [2]. The deal follows a series of plea agreements for dozens of defendants in the case [2].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on Civil Georgia alone; no court statement was read.

items.title: Georgia's Former Spy Chief Geladze Quits Interior Ministry for State Energy Board
items.lede: Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze signed the order Monday, ending a six-week stint, and pro-government media say he is moving to the oil-and-gas company's board.

sections.text: Georgia's former interior minister and State Security Service chief Gela Geladze has left his post as deputy interior minister [3]. Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze issued the order on 2 November [3]. Pro-government media reported he joined the three-member supervisory board of the state-run Georgian Oil and Gas Corporation [3]. He had become deputy interior minister on 15 September, a day after stepping down as security service chief [3]. OC Media also reported his departure after six weeks in the job [4]. No statement from Geladze was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the departure, which Civil Georgia and OC Media both report; confidence is moderate on the board post, which rests on pro-government media.

items.title: Georgia's Ex-Premier Garibashvili Pleads Not Guilty as Bribery Trial Opens
items.lede: The judge closed the rest of the trial to the public at prosecutors' request, citing Defense Ministry secrets, and his lawyer alleged pressure to confess.

sections.text: Georgia's former Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili appeared in person Monday as Tbilisi City Court opened the main hearing in his bribery case [5]. He answered "No" when Judge Tamar Mchedlishvili asked whether he pleaded guilty [5]. Prosecutors accuse him of taking an especially large bribe, as part of a group, while holding high political office, a charge carrying 11 to 15 years [5]. The judge granted a prosecution motion to close the trial to the public [6]. Prosecutor Ani Lekiashvili said the case concerns the Defense Ministry and could expose state secrets [6]. Garibashvili opposed the motion and called the case politically motivated [6]. Former Justice Minister Rati Bregadze was the only senior Georgian Dream figure in court [5]. After the hearing, lawyer Soso Baratashvili said Garibashvili told the court he faced psychological pressure to confess before the investigation began [7]. The lawyer asked investigators to open a torture case [7].
Confidence is moderate: the hearing, plea, and closure rest on Interpressnews alone; the pressure claim is the defense's account, and no prosecution response was found.

items.title: Georgia Fires Tbilisi's Gldani Prison Chief Amid Inmate Beating Probe
items.lede: The penitentiary service gave no reason, but the move follows reports that a jailed underworld figure was beaten by cellmates and hospitalized twice.

sections.text: Georgia's Special Penitentiary Service dismissed Ramaz Pirtskhalava, director of Gldani Prison in Tbilisi, on 2 November [8]. Nodar Kinkladze, head of Laituri prison in Guria, replaced him with the Justice Ministry's consent [8]. The service gave no reason [8]. The move follows an investigation into alleged assaults on inmate Davit Peikrishvili by cellmates [8]. Peikrishvili, linked to Georgia's criminal underworld, was hospitalized with multiple injuries on 19 and 20 October [8]. OC Media also reported the dismissal [9].
Confidence is high on the dismissal, reported by Civil Georgia and OC Media; the link to the beating case is the outlets' context, since the service stated no reason.

items.title: Georgian Dream Bill Would Scrap Random Recounts at Polling Stations
items.lede: The draft also shortens the time to certify results from 26 days to 15 and moves municipal tallying to the Central Election Commission.

sections.text: Georgian Dream lawmakers have introduced amendments to Georgia's Election Code in parliament [10]. The bill removes a rule that district commissions randomly pick up to five polling stations and recount their votes within six days [10]. It cuts the deadline to finalize election results from 26 days to 15 [10]. The Central Election Commission, not district commissions, would tabulate final municipal council and mayoral results [10]. Newly elected councils and mayors would take office on the ninth day after final results, instead of the 14th [10]. The bill also changes withdrawal deadlines for candidates and reporting rules for the State Audit Office [10]. No opposition or observer response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the bill's contents rest on Interpressnews alone, and the draft text in parliament's register was not read.

items.title: Armenia Says Border Talks With Azerbaijan May Fast-Track the TRIPP Corridor
items.lede: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said work on the US-backed route has effectively begun and accused Russian-linked circles of a plan to block Armenia's economic commitments.

sections.text: Armenia's Deputy Prime Minister Mher Grigoryan said the next stage of border delimitation with Azerbaijan will likely cover sections tied to the TRIPP transit project [11]. He said that work could move ahead of other border sections to speed up the project, though no date has been agreed [11]. He said officials are studying routes for a highway, a railway, and power lines in Syunik province [11]. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan told lawmakers his government has effectively begun implementing TRIPP [12] [13]. He said Armenia will order design work for the railway, highway, and power lines without waiting for a TRIPP development company [13]. He said a "secret plan" backed by circles in Russia and the Eurasian Economic Union aims to stop Armenia from meeting its economic commitments [12]. No Russian government response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on Pashinyan's start of design work, reported by Armenian public radio and 1news.az, and moderate on Grigoryan's and the "secret plan" remarks, sourced to 1news.az alone.

items.title: Pashinyan Says Armenian Guards Will Take Over All Borders From Russian Troops
items.lede: Russian guards still patrol stretches of the Iran and Turkey frontiers, and he gave no timeline, saying the shift needs a period of reform first.

sections.text: Armenia's Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said Monday that control of all the country's borders will gradually pass to Armenia's Border Guard Service [14]. He spoke at a joint meeting of parliamentary committees on the 2027 draft budget [14]. He said the handover will first require a period of reform [14]. Armenian guards have already replaced Russian border guards at Zvartnots airport, the Agarak crossing with Iran, and the Margara and Akhurik crossings with Turkey [14]. The handover on the Iran and Turkey borders is happening in stages, NEWS.am reported [14]. No Russian government response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the remark rests on NEWS.am's report of the committee session; no transcript or second outlet was read, and no timeline was given.

items.title: Germany Holds First Talks on Joining the British-Italian-Japanese GCAP Fighter Program
items.lede: Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said Berlin wants clarity very quickly on whether, and on what terms, it could take part.

sections.text: Germany's government is examining whether to join the GCAP fighter jet program with Britain, Italy, and Japan, Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said Monday [1]. He said first talks had already taken place [1]. Pistorius spoke in Berlin after meeting British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting [1]. He said he would hold more talks with the Italian and Japanese defense ministers in the coming days [1]. He said Berlin wants clarity very quickly on whether, and on what terms, Germany could take part [1]. Streeting said Britain would decide together with Italy and Japan [1]. GCAP is a planned stealth combat aircraft meant to replace Japan's F-2 and the British and Italian Eurofighters [1]. German media compare it with FCAS, the failed Franco-German fighter project [1].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on Der Tagesspiegel alone; tagesschau and Deutschlandfunk listings were seen but not read on this point.

items.title: Germany Drafts Emergency Cap on Gasoline and Diesel Prices
items.lede: The cap would last three months at most, and the ministry warns that setting it too low could halt fuel imports and cause shortages.

sections.text: Germany's Economy Ministry led by Katherina Reiche has finished a first draft law for a fuel price cap, tagesschau reported [2] [3]. The draft lets the government set a maximum pump price by decree as a last-resort crisis tool [2]. The cap would apply only after gasoline and diesel prices rise more than five percentage points faster than the average increase in other EU states for three straight weeks [2]. It would last three months at most [2]. German states could set different caps for local conditions [2]. The ministry told dpa that caps set too low could make deliveries unprofitable and halt imports [2]. Saarland Premier Anke Rehlinger, a Social Democrat, told Der Tagesspiegel the draft was a law to prevent a fuel price cap [2]. The party's economic policy spokesman, Sebastian Roloff, said it was not what the coalition agreed and must be reworked [2].
Confidence is high on the draft's contents, which ARD saw and Deutschlandfunk also reported. It is a first draft, and cabinet approval had not been reported by the cutoff.

items.title: Girl Hurt as Needles in Halloween Candy Spread to 11 German States
items.lede: Police said the needles appeared to have been placed deliberately, and they urged parents to check candy and keep any suspect items and their packaging.

sections.text: Police in at least 11 German states are now investigating Halloween candy spiked with needles and other metal objects [4] [5]. In Bremervörde, Lower Saxony, a 9-year-old girl cut her tongue on a pin at least 5 centimeters long hidden in a chocolate bar [4]. In Munich, a 9-year-old boy bit on a needle in a chewy candy but spat it out unhurt [4]. Two families in Essen also found needles in chocolate bars and gummies [4]. In Baden-Württemberg, two families in Filderstadt found needles in hazelnut bars on Saturday [6]. Police said the needles appeared to have been placed deliberately and could not be seen from outside [6]. Metal objects also turned up in wrapped wafer bars in Rielasingen-Worblingen, near Konstanz [6]. Police urged parents to check their children's candy and keep any suspect items and their packaging [6].
Confidence is high on the cases, which rest on police statements reported by tagesschau, Deutschlandfunk, and Stuttgarter Zeitung. No suspects were reported by the cutoff.

items.title: About 38,000 German Metalworkers Join IG Metall's First Big Strike Day
items.lede: Walkouts widen Tuesday in Baden-Württemberg, North Rhine-Westphalia, and Hesse, and no date has been set for the next round of pay talks.

sections.text: Germany's IG Metall union said about 38,000 workers joined 220 warning strikes and rallies on Monday [7]. It plans walkouts at more than 2,000 plants by the end of the week [7] [8]. The union plans to widen the strikes on Tuesday, focusing on Baden-Württemberg, North Rhine-Westphalia, and its Mitte district, which covers Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland, and Thuringia [7]. Workers walked out at Siemens Energy in Berlin overnight, followed by Mercedes-Benz, Rheinmetall, and Siemens Mobility [7]. In Baden-Württemberg, nearly 10,000 workers from 51 plants took part by 14:30, the union's regional office said [9]. Almost 2,500 of them were at Daimler Buses in Neu-Ulm [9]. The first strikes began just after midnight, when a no-strike obligation expired [10] [11]. The union wants a 5% raise over 12 months and job guarantees for about 3.7 million workers [7] [11]. Employers have offered a one-time payment and a 1.3% raise in July 2028 [7] [8]. Gesamtmetall chief Oliver Zander said the strikes do needless damage while Germany loses 10,000 industry jobs a month [8]. No third bargaining round has been scheduled [7].
Confidence is high that the strikes took place, reported by n-tv via dpa and Deutschlandfunk. Turnout figures come from the union and were not independently checked.

items.title: Merz Vows Zero Tolerance After Looting at Germany's Gen Z Rallies
items.lede: Frankfurt police counted 54 arrests and about 100 injured officers, and the chancellor said most young marchers were peaceful and named housing as a problem.

sections.text: Germany's 'Gen Z regelt' youth rallies in more than 30 cities stayed mostly peaceful on Saturday [12] [13]. Frankfurt police said Sunday they had made 54 arrests and recorded 87 criminal complaints [14]. About 100 officers were hurt, and five stores were looted [14] [15]. Hesse Interior Minister Roman Poseck said those arrested are 13 to 29 years old and mostly German citizens [14]. Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Monday that his government will show no tolerance for violence on German streets [16] [17]. His remarks come from a speech text for a closed CDU meeting, excerpts of which dpa and Reuters saw [16]. He said offenders will feel the full force of the law and thanked the police [16]. Merz also said most young people protested peacefully and named housing as a problem [16]. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius had questioned Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt's blame on "troublemakers from the migrant milieu" on Sunday [18] [19]. The organizers plan new protests on 20 November [20] [13].

Confidence is high on the Frankfurt figures, from a police and ministry briefing reported by tagesschau and Deutschlandfunk. The Merz quotes come from speech excerpts reported by tagesschau, citing dpa and Reuters.

items.title: German Teen Jailed Over Suspected Far-Right Arson Plot Against Asylum Shelter
items.lede: Police picked up a 15-year-old Friday night with a gasoline can, the date neo-Nazi chats obtained by NDR gave for an attack on a Winsen asylum shelter.

sections.text: Prosecutors in Flensburg, Germany, said Monday a 15-year-old is in pretrial detention on suspicion of preparing a terrorist offense [21]. Police in Lower Saxony and Schleswig-Holstein searched his home near Bad Segeberg and a 19-year-old's home in Winsen on Thursday [21] [22]. Both are suspected of conspiring to commit arson [21]. Police picked up the 15-year-old on Friday evening after witnesses saw him carrying a gasoline can [21]. Neo-Nazi chats obtained by broadcaster NDR discuss an attack on an asylum shelter in Winsen and name Friday, the night police picked him up, as the date [21]. NDR said it checked the chats and believes them genuine [21].
Confidence is high on the detention and searches, confirmed by prosecutors and reported by tagesschau/NDR and Deutschlandfunk. The chat contents rest on NDR's reporting alone.

items.title: Spam Flood Knocks Out Email of Germany's Left Party Lawmakers
items.lede: Each Left Party member got more than 20,000 emails, and the party says the attack is unrelated to the iPhone spyware warning sent to politicians.

sections.text: A so-called spam-bombing attack has flooded the email inboxes of Left Party members of Germany's parliament, the party said [23]. Each member has received more than 20,000 emails from many senders and in many languages, parliamentary manager Ina Latendorf told ARD [23]. She said the inboxes could no longer be used and staff were deleting messages [23]. Other parliamentary groups told her their members were not affected [23]. The Bundestag's wider email system saw only delays [23]. The federal cyber agency, the BSI, has been called in [23]. No one has said who is behind the attack [23]. The party said it is unrelated to the iPhone spyware warning sent to politicians [23].
Confidence is moderate: the account comes from the party via tagesschau, and no second outlet or BSI statement was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Germany Confirms Delays in Readying Its New H145 Combat Helicopters
items.lede: A cannon ammunition problem is to blame, Der Spiegel reported, setting back a 2.5 billion euro order for 62 aircraft that Airbus is due to finish delivering by 2028.

sections.text: Germany's Defense Ministry confirmed Monday that its new Airbus H145 combat helicopters will be combat-ready later than planned [24] [25]. The cause is a problem with the ammunition for the helicopter's onboard cannon, Der Spiegel had reported [24] [26]. Reports say the helicopter can fly but cannot fight for the foreseeable future [24]. The Bundeswehr ordered 62 of the helicopters from Airbus in December 2023 for about 2.5 billion euros [24][27]. Airbus is due to deliver the rest by 2028 and train the pilots [24]. Spiegel called the deal an early showcase for Defense Minister Boris Pistorius's plan to buy equipment already on the market [26].
Confidence is high: the ministry's confirmation was reported by Stuttgarter Zeitung via dpa and by Deutschlandfunk. No new readiness date was given in the material seen.
